bug_semantics: outfile_write() in src/outfile.c assembles a cracked-hash record into a caller-supplied fixed buffer of HCBUFSIZ_LARGE bytes by sequentially memcpy'ing username, then a separator, then the hash, then the plaintext, incrementing tmp_len after each copy with no remaining-capacity check. Default --show format is OUTFILE_FORMAT=3 (HASH|PLAIN). With --username, hlfmt_user_hashcat takes everything before the first separator as the username, so a hash-file line of nearly HCBUFSIZ_LARGE bytes yields a username that fills tmp_buf; the following separator/hash/plain copies then write past the allocation. At v7.1.2 HCBUFSIZ_LARGE is 0x1000000 (~16 MB) in include/common.h:130 and the --show sink is heap: potfile_ctx->tmp_buf from hcmalloc(HCBUFSIZ_LARGE) at src/potfile.c:152, passed into outfile_write at src/potfile.c:774/877/881. CWE-120 heap out-of-bounds write. PoC in hashcat/hashcat#4740: username of N-33 'A's plus a 32-hex MD5, --username --show.
flaw_origin: The CVE mechanism is the username-first unbounded assembly that runs together with the hash/plain copies, not the earlier mutually exclusive username branch. a460ab01b684eeb1d26c503df60d8654a57bf699 (2016-10-19, jsteube, 'Bring back --username handling to --show and --left') first wrote if (user_len > 0) { memcpy(tmp_buf+tmp_len, username, user_len); tmp_len += user_len; ... } immediately before the HASH memcpy, and deleted the old else-if (user_len) block that ran only when HASH was unset. Immediate parent f5a92900c6a0b032e73472017a909d4ee4bc18dd still has HASH memcpy at src/outfile.c:334-347 and username memcpy only in else if (user_len) at :349-364, so --username --show (default HASH|PLAIN) never copied the username. 26fd67d932ae80796c28bf620978530e7a54ee19 (2016-10-10) is the earlier conversion from fprintf-to-FILE* into unbounded memcpy into tmp_buf, including that exclusive username branch; it is the first buffer-copy class but not the first write of this advisory's sequential username+hash+plain path. 37175f5067ad67cc81564338aa4c684a99f04b39 (2023-10-07) only re-indented the already-present username-first memcpy into the non-JSON else and is a refactor, not a BIC.
